title: Spotify Alternatives: Free and Paid Options (2026)
summary: Spotify alternatives include Apple Music, YouTube Music, Tidal and Qobuz.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Can I move my Spotify playlists to another service?


Yes, and for most people the transfer is free or nearly so, but expect to fix some tracks by hand. Third-party transfer tools such as Soundiiz and TuneMyMusic read your Spotify playlists and rebuild them in the new service.


On the free tiers of both tools there's usually a cap on how much you can move at once. The bootstrap version is to transfer your five or six most-played playlists and let the rest rebuild as you listen.


Obscure remixes, podcasts and local files are the usual casualties, so a niche library means more manual repair.


### Which Spotify alternative pays artists the most per stream?


Treat any claim that they pay more, and any exact figure, with suspicion: neither Qobuz nor Tidal publishes a per-stream rate you can verify. Payouts also depend on the label deal and on how each service divides revenue.


If artist pay is your main reason for leaving, the surer move is to buy directly. Bandcamp sends a much larger share of each sale to the artist than any streaming service does.


A streaming subscription for discovery plus a few purchases a month costs more than streaming alone, but the money lands where you want it.


### Is there a good free alternative to Spotify?


Yes, but "good" means accepting ads and weaker controls. YouTube Music, Deezer and Amazon Music have each offered an ad-supported tier, though what's included changes often, so check the current terms before you commit.


Expect free tiers to limit skipping, offline downloads and audio quality. If you're leaving over price, a free tier is a fine place to start. Lossless audio and offline listening are what you'd give up, and both sit behind the paid plans.


### Will I lose my Spotify listening history if I leave?


You lose it inside Spotify's app, and no other service will import it. **Before closing the account, request your data export from Spotify's privacy settings.** It includes your streaming history as files you keep, even though no new service can use them.


To avoid starting from zero, connect a scrobbling service such as Last.fm to your new player, so your history keeps building from day one.
